messages:
maya: seeing intermittent 1-3% packet loss between rack-4a and rack-4b since ~03:05 UTC, spikes line up with LB healthcheck failures. GPUs in pool-gpu-2 getting preempted more often :grimacing:
netops-bot: detected interface flaps on tor-04 (phys port 12) 03:04:58 -> 03:09:03; flap count 5 in 5m
aj: ok grabbing pcap and stats, can you post the LB logs and which VIPs were impacted? :eyes:
maya: VIPs: gen-infer-01 and gen-infer-02, both fronted by internal L4 LB. LB logs show backend conn resets and higher RTTs to backends in rack-4b. snippet:
```
[03:06:12] backend 10.2.132.45 failed healthcheck: tcp timeout
[03:06:12] backend 10.2.132.47 failed healthcheck: tcp timeout
[03:06:12] failed backends 2/8
```
simon: can you run ethtool on tor-04 uplinks and also check MTU/ECN counters on host side? suspected ECN/MTU truncation issues from previous incidents.
maya: putting commands here, running now:
```
# on host gpu-node-27
ip link show eth0
ethtool -S eth0 | egrep 'rx_errors|tx_errors|rx_no_buffer'
# on tor
show interface te0/12 counters
```
nicole: also check for RDMA QP resets on the affected hosts, those can be sensitive to packet drops.
aj: results: ethtool shows small rx_drops and rx_crc errors bumping during spike window, MTU=9216 on hosts, tor ports report large 'fragmented' counters increasing. pcap shows TCP MSS negotiation ok but we see occasional IP fragments with DF set and don’t get proper reassembly.
maya: weird, hosts have jumbo MTU but ToR may be truncating due to intermediate device or misconfigured VLAN translation. could be ECN bits being cleared/tripping hardware bug.
simon: paste of tor counters and pcap md5:
```
Tor counters (partial): rx_errors: 0 tx_errors: 0 fragmented: 42
pcap md5: 9a3b...edf2
```
aj: next step: run iperf3 across racks with -M (set MSS) and also test with different MTU sizes to reproduce. can someone schedule quick netns iperf?
maya: running iperf now from gpu-27 -> gpu-46 (rack-4a -> rack-4b)
```
iperf3 -c 10.2.132.46 -P 4 -t 30
[summary] retransmits: 120 (bad)
iperf3 -M 1400 -> retransmits 3
```
nicole: that pretty strongly indicates path MTU blackhole or fragmentation handling issue. lowering MSS fixes it.
simon: is this only TCP? RDMA/payloads over RoCE also saw increased CQ errors earlier today. RDMA likely hit by packet drops.
maya: yes, RoCE counters showed QP resets correlated to same timestamps.
netops-bot: ticket created NET-1983: ToR tor-04 suspected hardware ECN/fragment handling bug. owner=@aj oncall=@simon
aj: temporary mitigations: 1) disable ECN on internal LB-to-backend connections 2) push mtu clamp on LB frontends to 1500 3) schedule trunk reconfig to preserve jumbo across leafs
maya: applied LB MTU clamp on gen-infer VIPs at 03:40 UTC, immediate drop in retransmits in 15m window.
```
iperf3 summary after clamp: retransmits 2, jitter low, latency stable
RoCE CQ errors dropped to baseline
```
simon: good. we should still replace tor-04 SFP or linecard during maintenance; hardware vendor has a firmware note about ECN+jumbo interplay on this ASIC family. filing FR to infra-planning.
nicole: also recommend running path MTU discovery tests from orchestrator to nodes and adding alert for fragmented counter > 10/min.
aj: created followup infra ticket INFRA-447 to replace tor-04 linecard and to test with vendor patch in staging.
maya: Thanks all — rolling monitoring rule and leaving LB clamp until hardware fix. will update INFRA-447 when vendor schedules. :thumbsup:
